segments: The 387th [year/page] of the Arab Kings.
He said to the envoy,
"Because the King of England (d'Ingilterra?) has recovered from illness,
he has need of fowls (pigeons/partridges?),
and he refreshes himself with delicacies."
Then Saladin clothed the envoy in royal garments,
and sent with him a great number of hens, partridges (or fowls?), and doves.
And after this,
three other envoys came from the Franks to Saladin,
and they asked for plums (or peaches/pears) and snow;
and they received them and left.
And it is said
that the purpose of the King of England in sending envoys time after time with these empty matters was not [merely this],
except only that he might accurately learn the strength of Saladin and of the counselors who were with him.
And when the battle grew fierce against the besieged (those inside),
they sent to Saladin and said,
"If help does not reach us,
behold, we will surrender the city."
And because Saladin,
apart from engaging the Franks in battle against himself,
was unable to do anything else,
the Franks divided into two parts:
one was fighting with those outside,
and the other against those inside.
And those inside, when they saw that they were already taken,
asked for a promise of their lives.
And the Franks said,
"We will not grant it,
except after Saladin gives us all the Frankish prisoners who are with him,
and restores to us all the cities that he took from us."
And when they sent to Saladin,
he said,
"I will give only three thousand prisoners in exchange for the Muslims who are in Acre.
And if they leave Acre to me,
I will give them a city in exchange for a city.
Otherwise, let them take it by the sword if they are able,
just as I took it—
that is to say, the rest of the cities."
And when the Franks heard this, they were no longer restrained,
but mounted ladders onto the walls,
and descended into the city.
And after they shed much blood,
they gathered those who remained into one quarter.
And those Muslims said to the Franks,
"Do not kill us
until we send to Saladin, so that he may ransom us with gold and with Frankish prisoners, as many as you desire."
